unresolvedItems.context: Procedure uses BASIC-style line numbers as statement labels. Allowed in VBA but rare in modern code. Parser must accept; migration can drop them.
unresolvedItems.suggestedNextStep: Parser accepts line numbers as optional leading tokens on statements; migration drops them entirely.

unresolvedItems.context: Legacy GoSub/Return pattern. Subroutine accesses procedure-scoped variables (sErr, vData, i) directly. No parameters or return values.
unresolvedItems.suggestedNextStep: Migration target: extract as private method that takes the row data and current state as explicit parameters and returns a validation result. The original implicit-state pattern does not survive translation.

unresolvedItems.context: Late-bound COM member access. Cannot resolve Workbooks.Open signature without binding to Excel type library.
unresolvedItems.suggestedNextStep: Migration target: replace COM Excel integration with OpenXML SDK (DocumentFormat.OpenXml) or ClosedXML for .xlsx, or with explicit Excel COM interop wrapper if Excel automation is genuinely needed.

diagnostics.message: On Error Resume Next at procedure top level. All errors are silently ignored unless explicitly checked via Err.Number. This is a serious code quality issue: errors in OpenRecordset, AddNew, Update, etc. will silently fail. Migration target should use try/catch with explicit error handling per operation.

Mixed return type: Variant function returns Long on success and String on failure (rows 430, 560, 580). Callers must check type at runtime. Migration target should use Result<int, string> pattern, exception throwing, or out-parameter with bool return.
GoSub/Return pattern at line 230 with implicit state sharing. Subroutine reads/writes procedure-scoped variables directly. Translation requires extracting as method with explicit parameters.

Late-bound COM (CreateObject + Object-typed variable). Member access cannot be statically validated. Migration target may need replacement library (OpenXML SDK for Excel) and explicit member checking.

Type-declaration character suffixes used: $ (String) on sFilePath, sErr; & (Long) on i, j, lRow, lCol. Modern style declares types via 'As' keyword. Equivalent semantically; migration normalizes to explicit types.
Line numbers used throughout (10, 20, 30, ...). Legal but archaic. Useful for legacy 'Resume <line>' patterns; this code does not appear to use Resume <line>. Migration drops line numbers.
Magic number: dbOpenDynaset = 2 used as literal at line 180 instead of named constant. Migration target should use enum.

GoTo-based control flow with multiple labels (NoExcel, OpenFailed, NextRow). Combined with On Error Resume Next, control flow is non-trivial to follow. Migration target should restructure as guard clauses with explicit returns.

SSN handling: code stores partial SSN as '***-**-' & Right(CStr(value), 4). Confirm intent: is full SSN being intentionally redacted on import, or is original SSN expected to be available elsewhere? PII handling may have compliance implications in state government context (HIPAA, state privacy laws).
